term: one-step causal coverage for nonroot individuals
definition: In the explicitly finite rootedEmpty model, rootedEmptyCauses world cause effect holds precisely when both individuals are present in that world, cause is the designated root zero, and effect is a distinct nonroot. RootedEmptyDependentCoverage requires such a cause for every present nonroot. RootedEmptyNoTwoStepCause prohibits any composable pair of these same-world causal edges. None of these clauses requires an explanation for the root, establishes a total PSR, compares worlds as temporal instants, or asserts well-foundedness of all imaginable causal relations.
note: Finite mathematical interpretation to test whether even strictly bounded causal chains force necessity. Its exception for the root is explicit and philosophically disputable; see docs/necessary-individual-empty-world-fork.md.
